# Three levels

**1. Bootstrap.** `clusters/nyx/flux/flux-system/gotk-sync.yaml` is flux-generated (`DO NOT EDIT`). It defines the `flux-system` `GitRepository` — `ssh://git@github.com/joker9944/k8s-config`, branch `main`, 1m interval — and a Kustomization reconciling `./clusters/nyx/flux`.

**2. The artifact.** `clusters/nyx/flux/nyx-manifests-sync.yaml` defines the `nyx-manifests` `OCIRepository` — `oci://ghcr.io/joker9944/k8s-config/nyx-manifests` — and a Kustomization of the same name, both in `flux-system`. It reconciles `./sync` inside the artifact, at a 30m interval with `prune: true`. Why there is one artifact rather than several is [a decision](/decisions/single-manifests-artifact.md).

The file is generated — `cue cmd --inject out=.. bootstrap ./clusters/nyx/flux` from `cue/` — and committed, because level 1 reconciles it out of git. It is the only place that names the registry.

`spec.verify` accepts only a keyless cosign signature made by [cue-publish](/workflows/images-and-ci.md) on `main`. The identity regex must spell the owner `Joker9944` — the certificate SAN carries GitHub's canonical casing, while `_registry` a few lines above is lowercase because GHCR normalizes image paths. Lowercasing the subject to match makes the artifact fail verification, with the artifacts themselves perfectly valid. The certificate subject carries the ref, so an artifact signed by a run from any other branch is rejected here — as is any artifact pushed by hand.

**3. Workloads.** One Kustomization per bundle, generated by `#Manifests.sync` and shipped inside the artifact under `sync/`. It carries the interval, timeout, prune, `sourceRef` and — the part that matters — `decryption.provider: sops` against the `sops-age` Secret.

# Ordering

Level 2 carries no ordering: it declares no `dependsOn` and sets no `wait`. All ordering is per-bundle at level 3, derived from capability declarations — see [capability graph](/architecture/capability-graph.md) for the registry, the chains and the cycle hazards.

The `sops-age` Secret is not read until level 3, so levels 1 and 2 going Ready proves nothing about whether the key is right or even parseable. `age-keygen -y` against the Secret's data is the cheap check; it prints only public keys.

# Traps

- **Only level-3 Kustomizations can decrypt.** `#Manifests.sync` is what sets `decryption`, so a SOPS file must live in a bundle directory inside the artifact, never at the artifact root.
- **A generated `kustomization.yaml` walks subdirectories.** Where `spec.path` holds no `kustomization.yaml`, kustomize-controller generates one — and it collects manifests from nested directories too, verified with `flux build`. This is why the render puts the level-3 manifests in `sync/` rather than at the artifact root: from the root, the level-2 Kustomization would apply every bundle a second time, without the decryption only level 3 carries.
- **Deleting a Kustomization deletes what it applied, all the way down.** `deletionPolicy` defaults to `MirrorPrune`, which with `prune: true` means delete: removing a level-2 Kustomization would delete its level-3 ones, and they their namespaces, PVCs and Postgres clusters. Levels 2 and 3 set `Orphan`, so a Kustomization leaving git leaves its objects running, and retiring a workload means deleting them by hand.
- **A hand edit on a Flux-applied object does not survive its next reconcile.** kustomize-controller removes fields owned by `kubectl` field managers, so a `kubectl label` on a bundle's Namespace is gone within one interval even where no manifest sets that field. Suspend the Kustomization first, or change git.
- **A capability-gated chart template renders only when helm-controller upgrades.** A template behind `.Capabilities.APIVersions.Has …` is evaluated against the cluster as it stood at the last install or upgrade, and nothing re-evaluates it afterwards. A CRD landing after a release installs therefore leaves the object missing indefinitely, and the next unrelated chart bump emits it — reading as a regression in that version rather than a deferred render. `helm get manifest --revision` per revision is what settles it. A `postRenderers` patch aimed at such an object needs an explicit `target`, because an inline patch relying on its own GVKN fails the entire render with `no matches for Id` wherever the gate is false.
- **`gotk-components.yaml` has two writers.** Renovate bumps the controller images in place; `flux bootstrap` regenerates the whole file from whatever version its CLI asks for. Re-running bootstrap without `--version` matching what is committed silently reverts the upgrade — the flag downloads the manifests for the version named, so the dev shell's CLI need not match.
- **`clusters/nyx/bootstrap.sh` is the whole manual procedure.** It creates the `flux-system` namespace and the `sops-age` Secret from stdin, then runs `flux bootstrap github`. Its `--version` is a literal that has to track `gotk-components.yaml`, or bootstrapping silently downgrades the controllers. It is not idempotent: `set -e` plus an already-present `sops-age` aborts it. The node taint is not its job — that comes from [nix-config](/platform/cluster-nyx.md).
